recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-40494 unless a future work-group decision reopens the broader inter-version compatibility policy.
issue_request: FHIR-40494 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core clarification for the Version Management Policy. It asked to finish the FHIR-38876 follow-up by making inter-version compatibility language about conformant resource instances/data representation, excluding non-normative content including STU content within normative artifacts, and scoping the listed changes to normative portions of the specification.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied by git commit 96bbb3012090ba09fd4c9f4cb2659881c77cdb9c, matching the Jira comment that cites Git master 96bbb30120. That commit edited source/versions.html to add the non-normative/STU caveat, move the normative compatibility paragraph, replace conformant-application wording with conformant-resource-instance wording for breaking and non-substantive changes, and phrase the change-kind list as applying to normative portions.
additional_context: FHIR-38876 is the immediate predecessor that added the adjacent warning that non-breaking spec changes can still break applications. Later, FHIR-41452 was an Applied/Persuasive R6 clarification implemented by PR #2944; its commits intentionally moved the change-kind definitions back to a general list, retained the non-normative/STU caveat with the normative paragraph, and added rare normative-breaking-change governance language. FHIR-51051 later changed only the datatype row in the same normative rules table.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current source/versions.html still defines breaking and non-substantive changes in terms of resource instances, explicitly excludes non-normative/STU content from the normative compatibility rules, and scopes the forward/backward compatibility rules table to artifacts that have become normative. Reintroducing the exact older 'normative portions' placement would conflict with the later FHIR-41452 structure without changing implementer understanding.

related_jiras.note: Predecessor Published issue that added the adjacent implementation-failure warning and left the data-vs-implementation framing to FHIR-40494.

Later Applied same-page datatype-rule update that leaves the FHIR-40494 compatibility framing intact.
